From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: SDK quickstart + env setup — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Sandeep / Alicia,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Fintrix's fraud screening flow and the places you're most interested in Redwood (structured extraction from claims, embeddings for historical matching, and a fast reranker for prioritized alerts). Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goals: reduce time-to-detect, surface high-confidence matches, and enable structured claim extraction into your downstream rules engine.
- Workloads: mixed real-time inference (low-latency) for triage + batch re-ranking jobs overnight.
- Constraints: PCI-adjacent data, want private VPC option or dedicated capacity; prefer simple auth and ability to test locally first.

What I attached / links:
- redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip — Python + TypeScript quickstart, env setup, and a tiny sample app.
- redwood-example-apps.tar.gz — simple embedding + reranker demos, with README for local testing.
- Drive folder (link below) with SDK guides and our integration MPA (fintrix-integration-mpa.pdf).

Initial engineering notes / guidance:
1) Auth & env: for early POC we recommend API key auth with REDWOOD_API_KEY + REDWOOD_API_URL (local or staging). For production, Dedicated/Private supports mTLS and OIDC/KMS integrations — we can scope that in the next call.
2) SDKs: we include both Python and TypeScript examples that demonstrate: generation, function/tool calling (structured output), embeddings.create, and reranker flows.
3) Routing & model variants: you can configure routing per-route in the SDK (host/model override) to send low-latency requests to a faster model and batch/rerank to a larger one. We'll share suggested routing policy for mixed workloads.
4) Local testing: quickstart includes a docker-compose and env template so engineers can run the sample app against a staging endpoint or a mocked local server.

Next steps I propose:
- Engineering sync with Dev (our infra engineer) + Rishi (solutions) to walk the sample apps and pick the initial integration pattern (30-45m). Proposed times: Mon/Tue next week.
- Fintrix to confirm whether you prefer Python or TypeScript as the primary POC language.
- I'll share a roadmap doc + HubSpot deal link for procurement steps.

Happy to adjust — LMK which POC language you prefer and a couple of times that work for your team.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — very helpful. A few clarifying Qs from engineering so we can prep before the sync: 

1) Auth — is the API key approach suitable for our early staging (we will not store card data but some PCI-adjacent metadata will be processed)? Also wanting to understand how switching to OIDC / mTLS later affects the SDK surface.
2) Embeddings + rerank — can the sample apps show the full pipeline: embeddings index, candidate generation, reranking step with a dedicated model? Any limits we should know about (dims, vector size, batch sizes)?
3) Structured output/tool-calling — we want to extract 6 specific fields from claims and have a deterministic mapping to our rules engine. Can we rely on function/tool-calling in the SDK for that, or should we use a secondary validation step?
4) Local testing — would prefer TypeScript as primary for our front-end team, but backend infra is Python. Can we run both examples locally and mock the routing to a staging host?

If you can surface short answers to the above before the call, that will help us be ready. Proposed times for a follow-up engineering call: Tue 10am PT or Wed 11am PT.

Thanks Sandeep — quick answers inline, and I pulled in Dev and Rishi to cover engineering/solutions details on the call.

1) Auth:
- API key: fine for staging and early POC. Use REDWOOD_API_KEY set in environment and connect to a staging REDWOOD_API_URL. Keys can be scoped per project.
- Production: switching to OIDC or mTLS is a configuration change on the control plane; SDK accepts token-based auth via Authorization header (Bearer) and supports client certs when running in Private/Dedicated. Dev can walk the exact steps on the call.

2) Embeddings + rerank pipeline:
- Example apps demonstrate: embeddings.create -> store vectors in a small local index (we include a sample using FAISS) -> candidate generation (ANN search) -> rerank call to the Redwood reranker model.
- Limits: SDK supports typical vector dims (256-4096) and batching; our sample uses 1536 dims. For production we'll recommend batch sizes based on latency SLOs — Dev can share tuned defaults.

3) Structured output / tool calling:
- Use function/tool-calling in the SDK for structured extraction. We recommend defining a strict schema for the 6 fields and using schema validation on the SDK side as a second safety net (our samples show the pattern). In practice teams use function calling + a lightweight post-processor to ensure deterministic mapping into rules engines.

4) Local testing / languages:
- Yes — both TypeScript and Python samples run locally. The quickstart includes docker-compose and an env template so you can point to a staging endpoint or a local mock server. You can override routing with REDWOOD_API_URL or per-request host/model override in the SDK.

Attachments & repos:
- redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (contains: README, examples/python/, examples/ts/, docker-compose.yml, .env.example)
- redwood-example-apps.tar.gz (FAISS demo, reranker demo, minimal UI)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/example-apps (includes full TypeScript demo and infra-as-code for local testing)

Proposed next step: Dev/Rishi and I will join Tue 10am PT to walk the sample apps and pick the initial routing model. Please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
